question: {}₁₈⁴⁰{Ar} { and } {}₂₀⁴⁰{Ca} are a pair of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Isobars**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isobars** are atoms of different elements having the **same mass number (A)** but **different atomic numbers (Z)**.
 
• In the given pair:
 
 
• **⁴⁰Ar**: Atomic number = **18**, Mass number = **40**
 
• **⁴⁰Ca**: Atomic number = **20**, Mass number = **40**
 
 
 
• Since both have the **same mass number (40)** but **different atomic numbers (18 and 20)**, they are **isobars**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1 – Isobars**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isotopes:**

 
 
• Same atomic number but different mass numbers.
 
• Example: ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl.
 
 
 
• **Isotones:**
 
 
• Same number of neutrons but different atomic numbers.
 
• For the given pair:
 
 
• ⁴⁰Ar: Neutrons = 40 − 18 = **22**
 
• ⁴⁰Ca: Neutrons = 40 − 20 = **20**
 
 
 
• Since the number of neutrons is different, they are **not isotones**.
 
 
 
• **Isoelectronic Species:**
 
 
• Species having the same number of electrons.
 
• Neutral ⁴⁰Ar has **18 electrons**, whereas neutral ⁴⁰Ca has **20 electrons**.
 
• Therefore, they are **not isoelectronic**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Isobars:** Same mass number, different atomic numbers.
 
• **Isotopes:** Same atomic number, different mass numbers.
 
• **Isotones:** Same number of neutrons, different atomic numbers.
 
• **Isoelectronic:** Same number of electrons.
